novelty_points.claim: 提出了一种基于图摘要的大规模时序图表示学习方法GSAERU，该方法结合图摘要技术和图自编码器，并利用循环神经网络学习时间维度的特征与依赖关系，能够高效生成大规模动态时序图的表征，显著降低内存消耗和训练时间。
novelty_points.claim_en: Proposed a large-scale sequential graph representation learning method GSAERU based on graph summarization, which combines graph summarization with graph autoencoder and uses recurrent neural networks to learn temporal features and dependencies, enabling efficient representation generation for large-scale dynamic graphs with significantly reduced memory consumption and training time.
technical_features: 将动态时序图建模为各时刻上原图快照的序列
利用图摘要技术对原图进行压缩，将压缩后的新图输入图自编码器，通过重构误差训练原图节点的表征
引入循环神经网络作为时序学习模块，学习原图在时间维度上的特征信息与依赖关系
在四个真实世界大规模图数据集上验证，平均内存消耗和平均训练时长分别仅为传统图神经网络算法的9.86%和13.27%
technical_features_en: Modeling dynamic sequential graphs as a sequence of snapshots of the original graph at each moment
Compressing the original graph via graph summarization and feeding the compressed graph into a graph autoencoder, using reconstruction error to train node representations of the original graph
Introducing a recurrent neural network as the time sequence learning module to learn feature information and dependencies of the original graph in the temporal dimension

Extensive experiments on four real-world large-scale graph datasets demonstrate that average memory consumption and average training time are only 9.86% and 13.27% of those of traditional graph neural network algorithms

novelty_points.claim: 提出了一种基于图摘要的分布式图神经网络优化训练算法DSGNN，采用“领导—工作者”工作模式，通过基于边分割的图流划分算法对原图进行划分，工作节点执行基于图摘要的小批量训练，并通过注意力层将结果汇总至领导节点，实现大规模图流数据上GNN训练的高效加速。
novelty_points.claim_en: Proposed a distributed graph neural network optimization training algorithm DSGNN based on graph summarization, which adopts a leader-worker mode, partitions the original graph using a graph flow partition algorithm based on edge segmentation, workers perform mini-batch training based on graph summarization, and results are summarized to the leader through an attention layer, enabling efficient acceleration of GNN training on large-scale graph streaming data.
technical_features: 采用“领导—工作者”工作模式，由领导节点划分图并分配子图，工作者节点负责训练
基于边分割的图流划分算法对原图进行划分，适应图数据的不规则性
工作节点执行基于图摘要的小批量训练，压缩子图以降低计算量
训练结果通过注意力层返回给领导节点，领导节点汇总并计算梯度，同步更新所有计算节点模型
technical_features_en: Adopting a leader-worker mode where the leader partitions the graph and assigns subgraphs to workers, and workers are responsible for training
A graph flow partition algorithm based on edge segmentation partitions the original graph, accommodating the irregularity of graph data
Workers perform mini-batch training based on graph summarization, compressing subgraphs to reduce computation
Training results are returned to the leader through an attention layer, and the leader aggregates results and computes gradients, synchronously updating models on all computing nodes

novelty_points.claim: 在分布式图神经网络训练中，提出了基于边分割的图流划分算法，用于将大规模图数据划分为多个子图并分配给工作者节点，有效解决了图数据不规则性导致的分布式训练难点，提升了训练效率。
novelty_points.claim_en: In distributed graph neural network training, a graph flow partition algorithm based on edge segmentation is proposed to partition large-scale graph data into multiple subgraphs and assign them to worker nodes, effectively addressing the difficulties caused by irregularity of graph data in distributed training and improving training efficiency.
technical_features: 基于边分割的图流划分算法将原图划分为子图，适用于图流数据场景
划分后的子图分配给各工作节点，实现并行处理
该算法能够适应动态图流数据的变化，提高分布式训练的扩展性
technical_features_en: A graph flow partition algorithm based on edge segmentation partitions the original graph into subgraphs, suitable for graph streaming data scenarios
The partitioned subgraphs are assigned to worker nodes for parallel processing
The algorithm adapts to changes in dynamic graph streaming data, improving scalability of distributed training

brief.paper_summary:
由于现实世界中的大多数数据都可以用图表示，因此近年来针对图表示学
习的研究越来越受到关注。通过将高维图数据转化成低维的表征向量，图表示
学习可以有效地对图的信息进行存储并快捷地访问图中实体的关键知识。利用
学习到的图表征数据可以为社交网络行为分析、节点分类、链路预测和聚类等
下游任务提供帮助。随着深度学习的快速发展，研究人员提出了基于图神经网
络的图表示学习方法，其使图中的节点能够同时学习图的结构信息以及邻域节
点的特征信息，从而得到高质量的低维表征。针对图神经网络上的图表示学
习，本文主要关注两个问题：大规模时序图场景下的图表示学习方法和分布式
场景下的大规模图的图神经网络优化训练方法。
真实世界中的图数据规模往往十分庞大且处于动态变化的状态，而现有的
图神经网络要么无法处理动态时序图上的图表征学习，要么面对大规模图数据
集时训练效率低下。为了解决大规模动态图上的图表征学习问题，本文提出了
一种基于图摘要的大规模时序图表示学习方法——GSAERU 模型。GSAERU 模
型由“图表征学习模块”和“时序学习模块”两部分构成。首先将动态时序图
建模为各时刻上原图快照的序列，接着在单时间步上将图快照输入图表征学习
模块。该模块通过图摘要技术对原图进行压缩，并将压缩后的新图输入图自编
码器，利用和原图的重构误差训练原图节点的表征。在获得单时间步上的图表
征后将其输入时序学习模块，并通过一个循环神经网络学习原图在时间维度上
的特征信息与依赖关系，从而得到大规模时序图的高质量表征。基于在四个真
实世界的大规模图数据集上的大量实验表明，GSAERU 模型能够高效生成时序
图的表征。与传统的图神经网络算法相比，其平均内存消耗和平均训练时长只
有其9.86% 与13.27%，且与性能最好的算法在大部分指标下的差距都不超过
3.5%。

ii
使用分布式技术加速神经网络训练也是如今热门的研究课题，因为在处理
大规模数据时，单个设备（如CPU，GPU）有限的内存和计算资源往往会成为
训练瓶颈。而分布式技术可以提供更多的计算资源来提高训练效率。然而由于
图数据的不规则性，传统分布式机器学习方法中的子任务划分和模型训练方法
难以直接应用于图神经网络。针对大规模图流数据场景下的分布式图神经网络
训练优化问题，本文提出了基于图摘要的分布式图神经网络优化训练算法——
DSGNN 模型。DSGNN 模型采用“领导——工作者”工作模式，首先由领导节
点利用一个基于边分割的图流划分算法对原图进行划分并将划分子图分配给各
个工作节点。工作节点随后执行一个基于图摘要技术的小批量训练并将训练结
果通过一个注意力层返回给领导节点，最后由领导节点汇总结果并计算梯度，
并根据梯度同步更新所有计算节点上的模型。基于四个真实世界的大规模图数
据集上的大量实验，结果表明DSGNN 模型可以大大加速GNN 模型的训练，
并且在链路预测任务上的F1 分数显著高于其它分布式图神经网络模型。

paper.abstract:
由于现实世界中的大多数数据都可以用图表示，因此近年来针对图表示学
习的研究越来越受到关注。通过将高维图数据转化成低维的表征向量，图表示
学习可以有效地对图的信息进行存储并快捷地访问图中实体的关键知识。利用
学习到的图表征数据可以为社交网络行为分析、节点分类、链路预测和聚类等
下游任务提供帮助。随着深度学习的快速发展，研究人员提出了基于图神经网
络的图表示学习方法，其使图中的节点能够同时学习图的结构信息以及邻域节
点的特征信息，从而得到高质量的低维表征。针对图神经网络上的图表示学
习，本文主要关注两个问题：大规模时序图场景下的图表示学习方法和分布式
场景下的大规模图的图神经网络优化训练方法。
真实世界中的图数据规模往往十分庞大且处于动态变化的状态，而现有的
图神经网络要么无法处理动态时序图上的图表征学习，要么面对大规模图数据
集时训练效率低下。为了解决大规模动态图上的图表征学习问题，本文提出了
一种基于图摘要的大规模时序图表示学习方法——GSAERU 模型。GSAERU 模
型由“图表征学习模块”和“时序学习模块”两部分构成。首先将动态时序图
建模为各时刻上原图快照的序列，接着在单时间步上将图快照输入图表征学习
模块。该模块通过图摘要技术对原图进行压缩，并将压缩后的新图输入图自编
码器，利用和原图的重构误差训练原图节点的表征。在获得单时间步上的图表
征后将其输入时序学习模块，并通过一个循环神经网络学习原图在时间维度上
的特征信息与依赖关系，从而得到大规模时序图的高质量表征。基于在四个真
实世界的大规模图数据集上的大量实验表明，GSAERU 模型能够高效生成时序
图的表征。与传统的图神经网络算法相比，其平均内存消耗和平均训练时长只
有其9.86% 与13.27%，且与性能最好的算法在大部分指标下的差距都不超过
3.5%。

ii
使用分布式技术加速神经网络训练也是如今热门的研究课题，因为在处理
大规模数据时，单个设备（如CPU，GPU）有限的内存和计算资源往往会成为
训练瓶颈。而分布式技术可以提供更多的计算资源来提高训练效率。然而由于
图数据的不规则性，传统分布式机器学习方法中的子任务划分和模型训练方法
难以直接应用于图神经网络。针对大规模图流数据场景下的分布式图神经网络
训练优化问题，本文提出了基于图摘要的分布式图神经网络优化训练算法——
DSGNN 模型。DSGNN 模型采用“领导——工作者”工作模式，首先由领导节
点利用一个基于边分割的图流划分算法对原图进行划分并将划分子图分配给各
个工作节点。工作节点随后执行一个基于图摘要技术的小批量训练并将训练结
果通过一个注意力层返回给领导节点，最后由领导节点汇总结果并计算梯度，
并根据梯度同步更新所有计算节点上的模型。基于四个真实世界的大规模图数
据集上的大量实验，结果表明DSGNN 模型可以大大加速GNN 模型的训练，
并且在链路预测任务上的F1 分数显著高于其它分布式图神经网络模型。
paper.english_abstract:
Since most data in the real world can be represented by graphs, research on graph
representation learning has attracted increasing attention in recent years. By transforming high-dimensional graph data into low-dimensional vectors, graph representation
learning can store graph information and access key information of the graph effectively. Utilizing the learned graph representation data can benefit downstream tasks
such as social network, node classification and so on. With the development of deep
learning, researchers have proposed a graph representation learning method based on
graph neural network, which enables nodes in the graph to simultaneously learn the
structural information of the graph and the feature information of neighboring nodes,
thereby obtaining high-quality and low-dimensional representations. For graph representation learning on graph neural networks, this paper focuses on two issues: graph
representation learning methods in large-scale sequential graphs and graph neural network optimization training methods for large-scale graphs in distributed scenarios.
The scale of graph in the real world is often large and keeps changing, and the
existing GNN models are either unable to handle graph representation learning on dynamic sequential graphs, or the training efficiency is low on large-scale graph. To solve
the problem of graph representation learning on large-scale dynamic graphs, this paper
proposes a large-scale sequential graph representation learning method based on graph
summarization—GSAERU model. The GSAERU model consists of two parts: ”graph
representation learning module” and ”time sequence learning module”. First, the dynamic sequence graph is modeled as a sequence of snapshots of the original graph at
each moment, and then the graph snapshots are input into the graph representation learning module at a single time step. This module compresses the original graph through

iv
the graph summarization technology, and inputs the compressed new graph into the
graph autoencoder, and uses the reconstruction error with the original graph to train
the representation of the nodes of the original graph. After the graph representation
on a single time step is obtained, it is input into the timing learning module, and the
feature information and dependencies of the original graph in the time dimension are
learned through a recurrent neural network, so as to obtain a high-quality representation of large-scale timing graphs. Extensive experiments on four real-world large-scale
graph datasets show that the GSAERU model can efficiently generate representations
of timing graphs. Compared with the traditional graph neural network algorithm, its average memory consumption and average training time are only 9.86% and 13.27%, and
the gap with the best performing algorithm in most indicators does not exceed 3.5%.
Using distributed technology to accelerate neural network training is also a hot research topic nowadays. The limited memory and computing resources of a single device
often become a training bottleneck when processing large-scale data. Distributed technology can provide more computing resources to improve training efficiency. However, due to the irregularity of graph data, the subtask division and model training
methods in traditional distributed machine learning methods are difficult to be directly
applied to graph neural networks. Aiming at the optimization problem of distributed
graph neural network training in large-scale graph streaming data scenarios, this paper
proposes a distributed graph neural network optimization training algorithm based on
graph summaries——DSGNN model. The DSGNN model adopts the ”leader-worker”
mode. First, the leader divides the original graph using a graph flow partition algorithm based on edge segmentation and assigns the divided subgraphs to each worker.
The workers perform a mini-batch training based on graph summarization technology
and return the training results to the leader through an attention layer. Finally, the leader
summarizes the results and calculates the gradient, and synchronously updates the models on all computing nodes according to the gradient. Based on extensive experiments
on four real-world large-scale graph datasets, the results show that the DSGNN model
can greatly accelerate the training of GNN models, and the F1 score on the link prediction task is significantly higher than other distributed graph neural network models.
keywords: graph representation learning,deep learning,graph neural network, distributed
technology

研究背景
图是一种通过节点集合与边集合来描述数据中的实体对象及其抽象关联关
系的数据结构，有着强大的非结构化数据的表示能力。因此图状数据有着相当
广泛的应用，如社交网络中用户的关注关系，电子商务平台中用户与商品的推
荐关系，金融领域中的账户汇款关系等，这些不仅与实际生活息息相关，也在
各自领域发挥着重要的作用。随着大数据时代的到来，大量的数据以非结构化
的形式涌现，截至2022 年，全球社交媒体用户超过46.2 亿，相当于全球总人
口的58.4%。其中Facebook 的月活跃用户数达到29.36 亿，微信月活跃用户达
到12.88 亿，YouTube 的潜在广告覆盖面为24.76 亿，TikTok 广告每月覆盖10.2
亿成年人，这些平台每天都在产生着数以万亿计的用户内容与交互联系，高效
地处理分析图数据能够帮助我们挖掘其中丰富的有价值信息，为研究与生产提
供新的视角和工具。因此在DB-Engines 统计的数据库流行趋势排名中，相比于
关系数据库、文档数据库等常见数据分析工具，图数据库是自2013 年以来增速
最快的分类。依据国际知名调研机构Gartner 的预测，全球图分析应用将以每
年100% 的速度迅猛增长，到2025 年使用图技术进行数据分析和创新的比例将
由2021 年的10% 提升至80%，包括图数据库管理系统在内的图技术市场将增
长到32 亿美元，复合年增长率为28.1% 。显而易见，对于大规模图数据的处
理和分析已经成为下一个技术创新的前沿领域，亟需针对于图数据的有效分析
手段。
针对这一问题，科研人员开发了各种图嵌入（Graph Embedding）技术来将
原始图数据转换为统一维度的向量，这些向量中保存着原图的拓扑信息，可以
用来为社交网络分析、节点分类、链接预测和聚类等下游任务提供重要支撑。
这一过程也被称为图表示学习（Graph Representation Learning）。经典的图嵌
入方法旨在将高维图数据的维度降低为低维表征，同时保留原图的拓扑信息。
它们包括基于线性方法的主成分分析（Principal Component Analysis，PCA）[1]
和基于非线性方法的等距特征映射[2]，基于随机游走的方法[3] 和基于矩阵分

近年来随着深度学习的普及，使用神经网络模型进行表示学习成为了研究

数据有着不相互独立的节点, 每个节点拥有不同数量的连接关系, 传统神经网络
中的一些重要操作无法直接应用到图数据，为了解决这一问题，图神经网络应
运而生。
图神经网络（Graph Neural Networks，GNNs）是一种基于深度学习处理图
数据的方法，它将图上的传播操作和神经网络结合起来，能够学习到图数据中
的节点与图结构的内在规律和更加深层次的语义特征，弥补传统深度学习在可
推理和可解释性的局限性。在实际应用中，基于图神经网络的图表示学习方法
表现明显优于其它传统图表示学习方法[5]。
尽管GNN 模型在处理图数据上展现出了优秀的能力，但如何高效地大规
模图数据上训练模型一直以来都困扰着科研人员。以训练GCN 模型为例，一
个节点的表征每次更新都需要递推式地依赖于其邻居节点的表征，这些节点
表征之间的运算会随着图的规模以及GNN 模型隐藏层数的增长呈指数级增
长，这会导致过长的训练时间以及大量的内存消耗。GraphSage[6] 在一个Tesla
P100GPU 上需要花费数小时时间才能完成Amazon 采购网络数据集（包含约二
百万个节点）的训练[7]。而VRGCN[8] 在一个Tesla V100GPU（16GB 内存）
上训练同样的数据集甚至会出现内存溢出的问题[9]。为了解决这一问题，科研
人员分别引入了采样和分布式计算的方法。通过采样可以在原图上得到一张规
模远小于原图的子图，利用采集得到的子图进行模型训练即可达到加速训练的
目的，然而采样得到的子图会不可避免地丢失原图的拓扑信息从而使模型的精
度下降。另一种方法是将分布式技术应用于图神经网络训练。然而由于图数据
的不规律性，很难将传统的分布式机器学习方法直接应用在图神经网络上，需
要根据图数据的特性重新设计分布式场景下的任务划分与模型训练模块。如何
在分布式场景下高效训练大规模图的图神经网络是一个值得研究的问题。
到目前为止，大部分的GNN 模型是针对不随时间变化的静态图开发的。
然而现实世界中的真实图数据规模往往十分庞大且处于动态变化的状态，例如
社交网络、金融交易网络和引文网络。针对动态时序图，如果仍然使用基于静
态图的图神经网络算法学习其表征，往往会丢失其时间维度上的特征信息和依
赖关系，使得学习到的表征质量不佳。为了解决这一问题，目前主流的解决方

1 . 2 . 1
大规模时序图表示学习的效率问题
在大规模时序图表示学习任务中，主流的解决方法是使用图神经网络与循
环神经网络相结合的框架。首先利用图神经网络学习单时间步上的图表征，接
着将这些表征输入循环神经网络中进行训练以学习其时间维度上的特征。然
而，无论是图神经网络还是卷积神经网络的训练都涉及大量的矩阵乘积计算，
当输入图的规模增大时，其训练时间也呈指数级增长，同时带来极大的计算资
源消耗。此外，由于循环神经网络要求输入数据的规模保持不变，而在时序图
场景中图中节点可能会产生增减，造成前后时间步之间数据规模的变化，使得
循环神经网络无法正常训练。
在大规模时序图中进行图表示学习，同时解决模型训练效率问题，具有如
下挑战：
• 如何对动态图进行建模，使得其能刻画图中节点与边随时间变化的动态过
程。
• 如何在不过分损失模型精度的情况下尽可能缩短模型的训练时间和节约训
练占用的计算资源。

分布式场景下的图神经网络训练问题
分布式图神经网络训练的工作流程一般分为三个阶段：1）数据划分；2）
GNN 模型优化；3）梯度聚合。其中梯度聚合步骤的过程与传统分布式机器学
习方法类似，而前两个过程由于图数据分布的不规律性，在实际实施过程中需
要考虑负载均衡，通信开销等具体问题。因此如何在分布式场景下高效训练图
神经网络模型具有如下挑战：
• 如何进行数据分区。数据分区是将输入数据（图和特征）分配到一组工作
节点中。首先考虑到负载均衡问题，每个工作节点应当接收到规模均匀的
子任务从而确保系统不会被某些节点拖慢整体训练速度，而图数据由于节
点分布的不规律性，难以像传统数据一样直接进行划分。此外，GNN 模型
训练时需要不断聚合目标节点的邻域信息，但在分布式场景中其邻域节点
往往会出现本地缺失的现象。如果忽视了这部分缺失的节点，模型的准确
性将会被破坏，如果需要获取目标节点的完整邻域信息，则需要向其它机
器发送请求，造成大量的通信开销，从而降低分布式训练的效率。
• 如何进行本地GNN 模型训练。由于数据的依赖性，工作节点进行本地模型
训练的方式与传统的深度学习训练方法有很大不同。在不访问其他工作节
点获取邻域信息的情况下，可能无法生成正确的计算图从而使得模型的精
度下降。如果采取允许访问其他工作节点的模式，又会带来通信协议选择
和隐藏层之间参数同步的问题。

主要贡献
1 . 3 . 1
基于图摘要的大规模时序图表示学习算法
本文对大规模时序图场景下的图表示学习进行了研究，在广泛调研现有方

基于动态图的方法
近几年来，针对时序图上的动态图表示学习问题引起了科研人员的兴趣。
现有的针对时序图的表示学习方法大多是由静态图上的方法拓展而来。
一种流行的动态图表示学习方法是将动态图中节点和边随时间的变化建模
为连续的点过程（stochastic processes）[21]。KnowEvolve[22] 和DyRep[21] 将
边随时间的增减建模为点过程函数，并使用神经网络将点过程函数参数化，从

中更复杂的变化模式——三元闭包过程，其描述了图中具有三个节点的三元组
从一对节点不连接的状态发展到任意节点两两连接的状态。模型基于所有的三
元闭包过程学习图中节点的表示。HTNE[24] 同样对节点的点过程进行建模，
另外加入了注意力机制来学习邻居节点对当前节点长期和短期的影响，最终根

模为以时间为参数的连续点过程函数，使得模型能够有效生成动态图的表示并
以此预测动态图的变化。

基于分布式的方法
利用图神经网络进行图表示学习可以得到高质量的表示，但随着图规模的
增大，其消耗的训练时间也急速增长。为了达到加速训练的目的，科研人员尝
试将分布式技术与图神经网络结合，并产出了许多优秀的成果，目前主流的分
布式图神经网络算法可以分为一下四类：
分布式全批量训练中分派子图方法：此类方法在每轮训练中对完整原图进
行训练。首先将图数据和待训练的GNN 模型输入领导节点，在训练过程中领
导节点根据具体的节点特征聚合任务分发给各个工作者节点进行计算，然后收
集返回结果并根据损失函数计算梯度，进行模型参数更新。NeuGraph[28] 通过
将每个顶点的特征平均分成多个部分来探索特征级并行性，从而以更细粒度的
方式划分工作负载。然后将其分配给不同的GPU 线程进行相应的计算。该方法
充分利用了GPU 海量的并行计算资源。ROC[29] 将GPU 内存管理转化为一个
成本最小化问题，它使用递归动态规划算法寻找全局最优解来决定每一块数据
应该缓存在哪个GPU 内存中以供重用。然而，由于只有领导节点保存模型参数
且训练时严重依赖于工作者节点的计算结果，导致这类方法的数据通信开销往
往很大，且每轮训练的运行时间呈现不规律性。
分布式全批量预处理子图划分方法：此类方法也是在每轮训练中使用对
完整原图进行训练，在得到输入的图数据和GNN 模型后，增加了预处理阶段
使领导节点将图提前进行划分，并将每个划分后的子图和一份GNN 模型的副
本发送给对应的工作者节点，由它们在本地进行GNN 模型的训练，最后将结
果返回领导节点，由领导节点汇总后再统一通知工作者节点更新模型参数。
DGCL[30] 分布式GNN 训练提供了一个通用且高效的通信库。它将最短路径
生成树算法运用到传输规划中，通过“避免竞争”的策略提高链路使用效率并
平衡不同链路上的工作负载。FlexGraph[31] 通过合并位于同一分区的相邻顶点
的特征以减少数据传输量。当每个计算节点收到来自其他节点的邻居信息请求
时，首先会在本地聚合部分邻居信息，然后将部分结果发送给请求计算节点，
而不是直接发送初始邻居信息。请求计算节点只需要将接收到的部分结果与其
本地节点进行聚合即可继续计算，这使得通信开销显著减少。然而，这类设计

量样本生成，从而提高了采样的性能。相较于前两类方法，本方法能够大大提
升训练速度，但整体模型的运行效率仍由领导节点的采样效率来决定。
分布式小批量联合采样方法：此类方法中领导节点不再对原图采样，而
仅仅只是划分原图，并将划分子图和GNN 模型副本发送给工作者节点。之
后由工作者节点在得到的划分子图上进行采样并将采样结果作为本地GNN
模型的输入进行模型训练。梯度计算和模型参数更新仍是由领导节点完成。
AliGraph[34] 在其系统中实现了四种不同的图划分算法，其能适用于大部分类
型的图数据输入。2PGraph[35] 提出了GNN 层次感知缓存。它采用固定顺序对
目标节点进行采样，这使得每个节点的训练顺序是固定的。通过在计算之前将
所有目标顶点的k 跳邻居预先缓存到GPU 内存中，几乎可以完全消除数据传输
的时间开销。这类方法的性能瓶颈在于领导节点的原图划分效率和工作者节点

研究动机
近年来，随着图表示学习（Graph Representation Learning）在社会科学、
生物学、物理学等领域的问题上取得了一系列成就，图神经网络（Graph Neural
Networks, GNNs）已成为了一个热门的研究课题。其主要通过深度学习技术学
习非欧几里得数据——图的拓扑结构与特征信息，并为图中的节点与边生成对
应的高质量表征，从而应用于链路预测、节点分类、图分类等下游任务。它在
网络流量预测、金融风险评估、社交网络信息传播等现实领域有着广泛的应用
前景。针对图表示学习的研究，科研人员已设计了许多经典且有效的图神经网
络结构[6, 10, 15]。然而在实际应用中还存着两个巨大的挑战。
第一，到目前为止，大部分的GNN 模型是针对不随时间变化的静态图开
发的。然而，现实世界中的很多图是随时间的推移而动态变化的，例如社交网
络、金融交易网络和引文网络。图3 1展示了一个用户与博文互动并相互关注
的动态网络，其中的每条边都有一个时间戳，这些动态行为传达了重要的信
息，可以挖掘出用户在时间维度上的依赖关系，帮助我们更好地预测用户未来
的行为。但如果只考虑静态图，这些信息就会丢失。
第二，尽管GNN 模型在处理图数据上展现出了优秀的能力，但如何高效
地大规模图数据上训练模型一直以来都困扰着科研人员。以训练GCN 模型为

约二百万个节点）的训练[7]。而VRGCN[8] 在一个Tesla V100GPU（16GB 内
存）上训练同样的数据集甚至会出现内存溢出的问题[9]。

为了解决在大规模时序图上进行图神经网络快速训练和预测的实际挑战，
本章节提出了一种新的图表征学习与时序预测模型，称为GSAERU，用于在大
规模时序图上进行表征学习和预测。GSAERU 模型由图表征学习和图时序学习
两个模块组成。在图表征学习模块，采用图摘要（graph sketch）技术将时序图
中每个时间步上的快照“压缩”成一组规模远远小于原图的图，并输入到一组
图自编码器（Graph Auto-Encoder, GAE）中进行学习，得到低维高质量表征，
达到加速训练大规模图的目标。在图时序学习模块，采用循环神经网络训练图
表征学习模块得到的表征，并输出预测结果，完成在大规模时序图上的训练。
基于在真实世界中的大规模时序图数据集上的大量实验，GSAERU 在加速训练
图神经网络训练和维持模型精度方面取得了突出的成绩。

4 . 1
研究动机
在深度学习领域，图神经网络（Graph Neural Networks，GNNs ）被认为是
处理图数据学习任务的有效方法，它可以将图结构信息融入到深度学习中，从
而取得明显优于传统数据挖掘方法和机器学习的效果。如今GNNs 已被应用于
现实世界中的许多领域，如社交网络分析[60, 61]，生物医学中的蛋白质结构分
析[62]，购物网站商品推荐[63–66] 和自然语言处理[67, 68]。近年来，研究人
员致力于GNN 模型的设计，开发了包括GCN[10]、GAT[15]、GraphSaint[7] 等
一系列流行的图神经网络模型。同时，为了提高GNN 模型开发效率，许多深
度学习库提供了GNN 开发的框架[69–72]。另一方面，为了达到加速训练的目
的，研究人员针对GNN 训练的优化提出了一系列新方法，包括新的GNN 运算
内核（Computation Core）[73, 74]，用于加速图数据计算的编程模型[75, 76]。
然而，这些优化仅仅局限于在单个机器上训练GNN，没有考虑到模型的可扩
展性。
如今，真实世界中的网络图规模往往会非常巨大，以社交网络图（微博，
微信）为例，其中包括上亿个顶点以及数十亿条边，而现有的大多数GNN 模
型无法处理大规模图数据集[77] 或效率低下。因此，如何提高图神经网络模型
在大规模图数据集上的训练性能对科研人员提出了新的挑战[78, 79]。一种较为
流行的解决方法是对原图使用采样[7, 9, 80] 或蒸馏[81–83] 技术得到一个规模
远小于原图的“子图”，并以子图作为GNN 模型的输入进行训练。这种做法
虽然能大大提高训练速度，但模型性能最后会取决于所采集到的子图的质量，
且由于子图会不可避免地丢失原图的结构信息，所以一定会导致模型预测准确
度的降低。另一种方法是将分布式计算与GNN 模型结合，因为在处理大规模
图数据时，单个机器的内存和计算资源是有限的，往往会成为限制训练速度的
瓶颈，而通过分布式计算能够调度更多的计算资源（如多GPU 集群）来提高

目前主流的子图划分模式分为离线模式和流模式[88]。离线模式是将完整图数
据一次性载入内存后再进行划分，而流模式是按批次读取图数据并实时地将节
点和边分配到其对应的子图中。对于大规模图数据而言，由于机器内存难以存
储完整原图，故使用流模式分割更为适合。
因此，本工作在DBH 分割算法[89]（Degree Based Hashing）的基础上引
入Count-Min Sketch 技术（详见2 . 2 . 3节）进行改进，形成了全新的流模式边
分割子图划分算法——Sketch-DBH。下面介绍DSGNN 框架中子图划分的具体
过程。

在上一节完成子图划分后得到了子图集合{P(i)|i = 1, . . . , K}，接下来需

DSGNN 模型进行了两项优化。
第一，对子图进行“扩展”。具体做法是对子图P(i) 中的每一个节点v，
查询最小堆minHeap 中的所有键值对判断是否存在该键。若存在则将节点v 的

的节点，而Sketch-DBH 算法是根据度小的节点计算子图的编号，这会导致这
些高度节点在子图划分后大量边的缺失。以至于在后续的GNN 模型训练中，
为了聚合其缺失的邻域信息而向其它工作者节点发送大量的查询请求，严重拖
慢模型的训练速度。而Sketch-DBH 算法中维护一个最小堆的目的就是实时保
存图流数据中的高频节点。

总结与展望
5 . 1
工作总结
本文着力于目前图表征学习领域存在的两大问题——“大规模图数据训练
耗时耗资源”与“传统方法难以训练动态图”。本文首先概述了图表示学习领
域的相关背景知识，随后对待研究的问题进行了介绍，并对目前针对大规模动
态图表示学习的研究工作和算法进行了整理。基于对当前研究工作中的优势与
缺陷的分析，我们设计了两种算法——“基于图摘要的大规模时序图表示学习
算法”与“基于图摘要的分布式图神经网络训练优化方法”。通过在多个真实
世界的大规模动态图数据集上进行了大量实验，我们验证了算法在加速模型训
练和减少计算资源损耗上的有效性。
对于“大规模图数据难以训练”的问题，本文首先调研了相关的解决方
法，发现现有的解决方法主要围绕两个方面展开：第一，使用采样技术从大规
模图中采集出一个规模远小于原图的子图并在其上进行模型训练，达到加速的
目的；第二，使用分布式技术，通过增加计算节点的数量来加快训练速度。然
而现有方法仍存在一些缺陷。对于采样方法，采样出的子图可能会丢失大量原
图的拓扑信息从而导致模型性能的降低，以及采样生成子图的过程是否可以在
线性时间内完成。对于分布式方法，分布在不同机器上的邻居节点想要获取对
方信息需要发起请求，过多的通信开销会给系统带来极大的负担从而拖慢训练
的速度。因此我们分别提出了基于图摘要的大规模时序图表征学习算法和分布
式图神经网络训练加速算法，通过图摘要技术中的局部敏感哈希对原图中的节
点进行映射从而得到一组规模远小于原图的图摘要。并通过在这些图摘要中
使用时序学习方法与分布式技术达到加速模型训练和减少计算资源消耗的目
的。通过在多个真实世界中的大规模图数据集上进行的实验显示了该方法的有
效性。
对于“传统图表示学习方法难以学习动态图”的问题，本文首先调研了动
态图表示学习的相关工作，发现现有的方法大多使用图神经网络与循环神经网
络相结合的方式来学习动态图的表示，随后我们总结了这类方法的通用框架。

58
第五章
总结与展望
然而在实际应用中，由于循环神经网络的结构特殊性，其要求图中节点不能出
现增减的变化，这就对动态图中节点增减这一情景做出了限制。因此我们提出
了基于图摘要的动态图表示学习方法，其将原图节点通过一个局部敏感哈希映
射到一个规模固定的新图中并学习新图的表示，最后将新图的表示作为循环神
经网络的输入进行时序特征的学习，解决了现有方法无法处理动态图中节点变
化的问题。大量基于真实世界大规模图数据集上的实验表明，本算法可以有效
处理动态图中的时序信息。
5 . 2
前景展望
近年来图表示学习在现实中的多个领域都已取得了引人注目的成绩，包括
金融、生物医学、社交网络，成为了解决链路预测、节点分类问题的有效方
法。然而，随着所研究图的规模日益增大，面对动辄数百万节点与上千万条边
组成的大规模图，传统的图表示学习方法往往不能有效对其进行训练，而引入
采样等技术对原图进行“压缩”后训练的方法又会不可避免地丢失原图拓扑信
息，从而使模型的精度下降。如何找到“效率”与“精度”之间的平衡点仍然
是一个值得研究的问题。
尽管针对图表示学习已经提出了许多有效的方法，但如何提高所学习到表
征的可解释性，即“如何判断训练得到的表征中每一维度特征所包含的具体信
息”仍然是一项具有挑战性的任务。
此外，本文的研究只针对图中节点级的表示学习，而没有对边级别的表征
乃至图级别的表征进行探索。在未来的研究中，将表示学习的范围扩大到针对
边乃至子图可能是一个可行的研究方向。

raw_evidence.interpretation: SG-JEPA targets the same problem domain as GSAERU: large-scale dynamic graph representation learning.

raw_evidence.interpretation: SG-JEPA emphasizes training efficiency and memory scalability, similar to GSAERU's claimed efficiency gains, but achieves these through a spiking embedding predictive architecture rather than graph summarization.
raw_evidence.quote: SG-JEPA avoids the complex machinery (negative sampling, graph augmentations, edge-level reconstruction, etc.), resulting in superior training efficiency and memory scalability compared with prior self-supervised dynamic graph baselines.

raw_evidence.interpretation: TGAE uses a temporal graph autoencoder, overlapping with GSAERU's use of graph autoencoders for temporal graphs, but for graph generation rather than node representation learning.

conclusions.summary: 基于提供的有效证据卡，GSAERU 所提出的“图摘要压缩 + 图自编码器重构误差 + 循环神经网络时序模块”完整技术组合在现有检索覆盖内未被任何单篇文献完整公开。检索到的两篇相关文献（TGAE、SG-JEPA）分别涉及图自编码器处理时序图快照和大规模动态图表示学习，但均未同时组合图摘要、自编码器重构误差与独立RNN时序模块，故仅构成部分重叠。由于检索覆盖执行情况未知且申请人原始论文未纳入对照，无法完全排除已有类似公开，因此新颖性判定为部分新颖。
conclusions.verdict_reason: 综合两张单卡核验结果：card_62cce85b10e07492d6d66e87（TGAE）与 card_3d9d0903795629dfa516c9a7（SG-JEPA）均仅部分重叠，未公开 GSAERU 的完整技术组合（图摘要压缩+图自编码器重构误差+RNN时序模块）。TGAE 使用图自编码器处理快照序列但面向图模拟生成，不含图摘要与RNN；SG-JEPA 面向大规模动态图表示学习但采用脉冲联合嵌入预测架构，明确未使用图摘要、重构误差与独立RNN时序模块。两篇均不能视为单篇完整公开该组合，故不构成先占性公开。但存在关键证据缺口：未核验申请人原始论文（GSAERU 自身）作为对照，且未检索到任何同时组合图摘要+图自编码器+RNN的文献，无法完全排除他人已公开类似组合。因此判定为部分新颖，置信度中等。

conclusions.summary: 基于有效证据卡，DSGNN 的“领导—工作者模式 + 边分割图流划分 + 图摘要小批量训练 + 注意力层结果聚合”完整技术组合未在任何单篇文献中完整公开。检索到的 AGL、AliGraph、GraphSAINT 均仅部分覆盖该框架的个别特征（分别涉及分布式训练、图采样小批量训练等），但都缺少图摘要压缩、leader-worker工作模式及注意力聚合等核心要素，因此无法构成先占性公开。由于检索覆盖执行未知且缺少直接针对该组合的文献，新颖性判定为部分新颖。
conclusions.verdict_reason: 综合核验的3篇文献（AGL、AliGraph、GraphSAINT）均仅部分覆盖DSGNN的某些技术特征，未有任何单篇公开完整组合。AGL覆盖分布式GNN训练但缺少leader-worker、边分割图流划分、图摘要小批量训练和注意力层汇总；AliGraph为工业系统，覆盖分布式训练但未涉及任何核心特征；GraphSAINT覆盖基于子图的小批量训练但非分布式且为图采样而非图摘要，亦无leader-worker、边分割划分和注意力聚合。这些文献分别公开了部分特征，但多篇分别公开不等于单篇完整公开，不能据此否定新颖性。现有证据不足以证实或否定DSGNN四个特征组合的完整公开，故判定为partially_novel，置信度较低。

Abstract.

Dynamic graph learning aims to capture evolving structural and semantic patterns in real-world systems, such as fraud detection and recommender systems. Due to the scarcity of labeled data in real-world dynamic graphs, recent studies have introduced generative or contrastive paradigms (e.g., masked graph autoencoders or graph contrastive learning) to generate task-agnostic graph embeddings. However, these methods typically rely on complex edge-level reconstruction objectives and tailored graph augmentation strategies. It incurs substantial computational overhead when scaling to large-scale dynamic graphs.
In this paper, we propose SG-JEPA, a joint spiking embedding predictive architecture for large-scale dynamic graphs. In contrast to existing self-supervised methods, SG-JEPA partitions nodes into context and target sets along the temporal dimension to learn embeddings that are predictive of each other via additional spatial-temporal information. Furthermore, through encoding sequential inputs into coarse-to-fine spike count embeddings, spiking neurons enable SG-JEPA to adapt to the varying computational constraints of downstream tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SG-JEPA achieves competitive or even superior performance over discriminative baselines on node classification, while effectively scaling to the dynamic graph with 13 million edges. SG-JEPA avoids the complex machinery (negative sampling, graph augmentations, edge-level reconstruction, etc.), resulting in superior training efficiency and memory scalability compared with prior self-supervised dynamic graph baselines.

Keywords: Dynamic Graphs, Graph Neural Networks, Self-Supervised, Spiking Neural Networks

1. Introduction

Graphs are a fundamental data structure for modeling complex relational systems, ranging from social interactions to traffic systems. In many real-world scenarios, some systems evolving over time can be modeled as dynamic graphs that encode both structural and tem

The generation of voluminous scientific data poses significant challenges for efficient storage, transfer, and analysis. Recently, error-bounded lossy compression methods emerged due to their ability to achieve high compression ratios while controlling data distortion. However, they often overlook the inherent spatial and temporal correlations within scientific data, thus missing opportunities for higher compression. In this paper we propose GRAPHCOMP, a novel graph-based method for error-bounded lossy compression of scientific data. We perform irregular segmentation of the original grid data and generate a graph representation that preserves the spatial and temporal correlations. Inspired by Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), we then propose a temporal graph autoencoder to learn latent representations that significantly reduce the size of the graph, effectively compressing the original data. Decompression reverses the process and utilizes the learnt graph model together with the latent representation to reconstruct an approximation of the original data. The decompressed data are guaranteed to satisfy a user-defined point-wise error bound. We compare our method against the state-of-the-art error-bounded lossy methods (i.e., HPEZ, SZ3.1, SPERR, and ZFP) on large-scale real and synthetic data. GRAPHCOMP consistently achieves the highest compression ratio across most datasets, outperforming the second-best method by margins ranging from 22% to 50%.

Purpose: Over 5M+ people in India rely on Indian Sign Language for communication with specially-abled people, and yet technological support remains very limited. We developed a real-time ISL recognition system as a proof-of-concept demonstrating CPU-based deployment feasibility. Methods: We adapted and optimized existing HWGAT architecture with 9.7M parameters (52.7% reduction from baseline) processing 29 MediaPipe-extracted keypoints enhanced with Fourier features, cyclic shifts, and learnable positional encodings. Our heuristic motion-gated mechanism uses simple displacement thresholds for continuous sign detection. Results: On a limited 6-class dataset (76 samples), the system achieved 78.57% validation accuracy. The 95% CI (49.2%-95.3%) reflects higher variance due to a small sample size, which indicates that the results should be interpreted as preliminary. Ablation studies show that incremental improvements are as such: learnable encodings (+8.33%), Fourier features (+7.14%), and cyclic shifts (+7.14%). Conclusion: Our work demonstrates the feasibility of a CPU-based ISL recognition but acknowledges its significant limitations: a small vocabulary, limited amount of training data and simpler motion-gating heuristics. Findings established baseline for future large-scale studies.

Abstract.

Accurate traffic flow forecasting is a crucial research topic in transportation management. However, it is a challenging problem due to rapidly changing traffic conditions, high nonlinearity of traffic flow, and complex spatial and temporal correlations of road networks.
Most existing studies either try to capture the spatial dependencies between roads using the same semantic graph over different time steps, or assume all sensors on the roads are equally likely to be connected regardless of the distance between them. However, we observe that the spatial dependencies between roads indeed change over time, and two distant roads are not likely to be helpful to each other when predicting the traffic flow, both of which limit the performance of existing studies.
In this paper, we propose Temporal Graph Learning Recurrent Neural Network (TGLRN) to address these problems.
More precisely, to effectively model the nature of time series, we leverage Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to dynamically construct a graph at each time step, thereby capturing the time-evolving spatial dependencies between roads (i.e., microscopic view). Simultaneously, we provide the Adaptive Structure Information to the model, ensuring that close and consecutive sensors are considered to be more important for predicting the traffic flow (i.e., macroscopic view).
Furthermore, to endow TGLRN with robustness, we introduce an edge sampling strategy when constructing the graph at each time step, which eventually leads to further improvements on the model performance.
Experimental results on four commonly used real-world benchmark datasets show the effectiveness of TGLRN.

Graph simulation has recently received a surge of attention in graph processing and analytics. In real-life applications, e.g. social science, biology, and chemistry, many graphs are composed of a series of evolving graphs (i.e., temporal graphs). While most of the existing graph generators focus on static graphs, the temporal information of the graphs is ignored. In this paper, we focus on simulating temporal graphs, which aim to reproduce the structural and temporal properties of the observed real-life temporal graphs. In this paper, we first give an overview of the existing temporal graph generators, including recently emerged learning-based approaches. Most of these learning-based methods suffer from one of the limitations: low efficiency in training or slow generating, especially for temporal random walk-based methods. Therefore, we propose an efficient learning-based approach to generate graph snapshots, namely temporal graph autoencoder (TGAE). Specifically, we propose an attention-based graph encoder to encode temporal and structural characteristics on sampled ego-graphs. And we proposed an ego-graph decoder that can achieve a good trade-off between simulation quality and efficiency in temporal graph generation. Finally, the experimental evaluation is conducted among our proposed TGAE and representative temporal graph generators on real-life temporal graphs and synthesized graphs. It is reported that our proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art temporal graph generators by means of simulation quality and efficiency.

Abstract

Dynamic graphs are widely used to represent evolving real-world networks. Temporal Graph Neural Networks (TGNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for processing such graphs, but the lack of transparency and explainability limits their practical adoption. Research on TGNN explainability is still in its early stages and faces several key issues: (i) Current methods are tailored to specific TGNN types, restricting generality. (ii) They suffer from high computational costs, making them unsuitable for large-scale networks. (iii) They often overlook the structural connectivity of explanations and require prior knowledge, reducing user-friendliness. Abstract

With the process of urbanization and the rapid growth of population, the issue of traffic congestion has become an increasingly critical concern. Intelligent transportation systems heavily rely on real-time and precise prediction algorithms to address this problem. While Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) methods in deep learning have demonstrated high accuracy in predicting road conditions when sufficient data is available, forecasting in road networks with limited data remains a challenging task. This study proposed a novel Spatial-temporal Convolutional Network (TL-GPSTGN) based on graph pruning and transfer learning framework to tackle this issue. Firstly, the essential structure and information of the graph are extracted by analyzing the correlation and information entropy of the road network structure and feature data. By utilizing graph pruning techniques, the adjacency matrix of the graph and the input feature data are processed, resulting in a significant improvement in the model’s migration perfo

poral dependencies. To capture such evolving patterns, Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) are proposed to integrate graph representation learning with temporal modeling, which have achieved strong performance across tasks such as link prediction and node classification (Skarding et al., 2021; Feng et al., 2025). Different from vanilla static GNNs, DGNNs continuously update node representations by incorporating temporal information from evolving interactions or graph snapshots (Yu et al., 2023; Li et al., 2024; Zhu et al., 2024). However, most DGNNs tailored for supervised or semi-supervised settings rely heavily on labeled data, which is often scarce or expensive to obtain in real-world applications.

Figure 1. Illustration of self-supervised learning frameworks for DGNNs. (a) Contrastive-based methods construct multiple augmented temporal graph views and align representations across different views via contrastive objectives, which rely on well-designed graph augmentation strategies. (b) Generative-based methods learn representations by reconstructing masked edges or temporal signals through decoder networks. They often incur high computational and memory overhead on large-scale dynamic graphs. (c) Joint-embedding predictive architecture models temporal evolution by predicting target node representations from historical context representations directly in embedding space.

This limitation motivates the exploration of self-supervised paradigms for dynamic graph representation learning. Recent efforts attempt to alleviate label dependency by introducing contrastive or generative objectives for dynamic graphs. Contrastive methods construct multiple graph views through structural perturbations or temporal subgraph sampling, and then maximize agreement between representations of positive pairs while repelling negatives (Jiang et al., 2021; Alomrani et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2023). Although effective, such approaches typically rely on carefully designed graph augmentations and negative sampling strategies. As shown in Figure 1, it introduces substantial computational overhead and inductive biases. Inspired by masked autoencoders, generative methods tend to reconstruct masked edges or temporal signals from partial observations (He et al., 2025). While they avoid explicit negative sampling, reconstruction-based objectives often emphasize low-level structural fidelity and incur computational cost when scaling to large dynamic graphs. More importantly, the choice of effective augmentations (e.g., edge modification or node feature masking) is often task-dependent and requires careful manual selection, which limits adaptability and scalability in real-world dynamic graphs.

Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), as an emerging alternative, was recently proposed in computer vision as a non-generative framework for learning semantic representations (Assran et al., 2023; Bardes et al., 2023; Assran et al., 2025). Instead of reconstructing raw inputs or enforcing invariance across augmented views, JEPA learns representations that are predictive of each other when conditioned on additional latent information. By performing prediction directly in representation space, JEPA avoids pixel-level reconstruction and reduces reliance on handcrafted augmentations, leading to improved scalability and semantic abstraction.
Although JEPA has demonstrated strong performance in image modeling, its potential in dynamic graph learning remains largely underexplored. We believe that the predictive learning principle of JEPA naturally aligns with the temporal evolution in dynamic graphs, where representations at different time steps should be mutually predictive under spatio-temporal conditioning. However, directly extending it to dynamic graph representation learning is non-trivial.We identify two key challenges in applying JEPA to dynamic graphs.

Due to the rapid growth of scientific publications, identifying all related reference articles in the literature has become increasingly challenging yet highly demanding. Existing methods primarily assess candidate publications from a static perspective, focusing on the content of articles and their structural information, such as citation relationships. There is a lack of research regarding how to account for the evolving impact among papers on their embeddings. Toward this goal, this paper introduces a temporal dimension to paper recommendation strategies. The core idea is to continuously update a paper's embedding when new citation relationships appear, enhancing its relevance for future recommendations. Whenever a citation relationship is added to the literature upon the publication of a paper, the embeddings of the two related papers are updated through a Temporal Graph Neural Network (TGN). A learnable memory update module based on a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) is utilized to study the evolution of the embedding of a paper in order to predict its reference impact in a future timestamp. Such a TGN-based model learns a pattern of how people's views of the paper may evolve, aiming to guide paper recommendations more precisely. Extensive experiments on an open citation network dataset, including 313,278 articles from https://paperswithcode.com/about PaperWithCode, have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Fault location in distribution grids is critical for reliability and minimizing outage durations. Yet, it remains challenging due to partial observability, given sparse measurement infrastructure. Recent works show promising results by combining Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for spatio-temporal learning. Still, many modern GNN architectures remain untested for this grid application, while existing GNN solutions have not explored GNN topology definitions beyond simply adopting the full grid topology to construct the GNN graph. We address these gaps by (i) systematically comparing a newly proposed graph-forming strategy (measured-only) to the traditional full-topology approach, and (ii) introducing STGNN (Spatio-temporal GNN) models based on GraphSAGE and an improved Graph Attention (GATv2), for distribution grid fault location; (iii) benchmarking them against state-of-the-art STGNN and RNN baselines on the IEEE 123-bus feeder. In our experiments, all evaluated STGNN variants achieve high performance and consistently outperform a pure RNN baseline, with improvements up to 11 percentage points F1. Among STGNN models, the newly explored RGATv2 and RGSAGE achieve only marginally higher F1 scores. Still, STGNNs demonstrate superior stability, with tight confidence intervals (within +/- 1.4%) compared to the RNN baseline (up to +/- 7.5%) across different experiment runs. Finally, our proposed reduced GNN topology (measured-only) shows clear benefits in both (i) model training time (6-fold reduction) and (ii) model performance (up to 11 points F1). This suggests that measured-only graphs offer a more practical, efficient, and robust framework for partially observable distribution grids.

Abstract.

Dynamic graph learning aims to capture evolving structural and semantic patterns in real-world systems, such as fraud detection and recommender systems. Due to the scarcity of labeled data in real-world dynamic graphs, recent studies have introduced generative or contrastive paradigms (e.g., masked graph autoencoders or graph contrastive learning) to generate task-agnostic graph embeddings. However, these methods typically rely on complex edge-level reconstruction objectives and tailored graph augmentation strategies. It incurs substantial computational overhead when scaling to large-scale dynamic graphs.
In this paper, we propose SG-JEPA, a joint spiking embedding predictive architecture for large-scale dynamic graphs. In contrast to existing self-supervised methods, SG-JEPA partitions nodes into context and target sets along the temporal dimension to learn embeddings that are predictive of each other via additional spatial-temporal information. Furthermore, through encoding sequential inputs into coarse-to-fine spike count embeddings, spiking neurons enable SG-JEPA to adapt to the varying computational constraints of downstream tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SG-JEPA achieves competitive or even superior performance over discriminative baselines on node classification, while effectively scaling to the dynamic graph with 13 million edges. SG-JEPA avoids the complex machinery (negative sampling, graph augmentations, edge-level reconstruction, etc.), resulting in superior training efficiency and memory scalability compared with prior self-supervised dynamic graph baselines.

Keywords: Dynamic Graphs, Graph Neural Networks, Self-Supervised, Spiking Neural Networks

source_records.abstract: Dynamic graphs are widely used to represent evolving real-world networks. Temporal Graph Neural Networks (TGNNs) have emerged as a powerful tool for processing such graphs, but the lack of transparency and explainability limits their practical adoption. Research on TGNN explainability is still in its early stages and faces several key issues: (i) Current methods are tailored to specific TGNN types, restricting generality. (ii) They suffer from high computational costs, making them unsuitable for large-scale networks. (iii) They often overlook the structural connectivity of explanations and require prior knowledge, reducing user-friendliness. To address these issues, we propose GRExplainer, the first universal, efficient, and user-friendly explanation method for TGNNs. GRExplainer extracts node sequences as a unified feature representation, making it independent of specific input formats and thus applicable to both snapshot-based and event-based TGNNs (the major types of TGNNs). By utilizing breadth-first search and temporal information to construct input node sequences, GRExplainer reduces redundant computation and improves efficiency. To enhance user-friendliness, we design a generative model based on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), enabling automated and continuous explanation generation. Experiments on six real-world datasets with three target TGNNs show that GRExplainer outperforms existing baseline methods in generality, efficiency, and user-friendliness.
source_records.title: GRExplainer: A Universal Explanation Method for Temporal Graph Neural Networks

source_records.abstract: The generation of voluminous scientific data poses significant challenges for efficient storage, transfer, and analysis. Recently, error-bounded lossy compression methods emerged due to their ability to achieve high compression ratios while controlling data distortion. However, they often overlook the inherent spatial and temporal correlations within scientific data, thus missing opportunities for higher compression. In this paper we propose GRAPHCOMP, a novel graph-based method for error-bounded lossy compression of scientific data. We perform irregular segmentation of the original grid data and generate a graph representation that preserves the spatial and temporal correlations. Inspired by Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), we then propose a temporal graph autoencoder to learn latent representations that significantly reduce the size of the graph, effectively compressing the original data. Decompression reverses the process and utilizes the learnt graph model together with the latent representation to reconstruct an approximation of the original data. The decompressed data are guaranteed to satisfy a user-defined point-wise error bound. We compare our method against the state-of-the-art error-bounded lossy methods (i.e., HPEZ, SZ3.1, SPERR, and ZFP) on large-scale real and synthetic data. GRAPHCOMP consistently achieves the highest compression ratio across most datasets, outperforming the second-best method by margins ranging from 22% to 50%.
source_records.title: GraphComp: Extreme Error-bounded Compression of Scientific Data via Temporal Graph Autoencoders

source_records.abstract: With the process of urbanization and the rapid growth of population, the issue of traffic congestion has become an increasingly critical concern. Intelligent transportation systems heavily rely on real-time and precise prediction algorithms to address this problem. While Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) methods in deep learning have demonstrated high accuracy in predicting road conditions when sufficient data is available, forecasting in road networks with limited data remains a challenging task. This study proposed a novel Spatial-temporal Convolutional Network (TL-GPSTGN) based on graph pruning and transfer learning framework to tackle this issue. Firstly, the essential structure and information of the graph are extracted by analyzing the correlation and information entropy of the road network structure and feature data. By utilizing graph pruning techniques, the adjacency matrix of the graph and the input feature data are processed, resulting in a significant improvement in the model's migration performance. Subsequently, the well-characterized data are inputted into the spatial-temporal graph convolutional network to capture the spatial-temporal relationships and make predictions regarding the road conditions. Furthermore, this study conducts comprehensive testing and validation of the TL-GPSTGN method on real datasets, comparing its prediction performance against other commonly used models under identical conditions. The results demonstrate the exceptional predictive accuracy of TL-GPSTGN on a single dataset, as well as its robust migration performance across different datasets.
source_records.title: Graph Pruning Based Spatial and Temporal Graph Convolutional Network with Transfer Learning for Traffic Prediction

source_records.abstract: Accurate traffic flow forecasting is a crucial research topic in transportation management. However, it is a challenging problem due to rapidly changing traffic conditions, high nonlinearity of traffic flow, and complex spatial and temporal correlations of road networks. Most existing studies either try to capture the spatial dependencies between roads using the same semantic graph over different time steps, or assume all sensors on the roads are equally likely to be connected regardless of the distance between them. However, we observe that the spatial dependencies between roads indeed change over time, and two distant roads are not likely to be helpful to each other when predicting the traffic flow, both of which limit the performance of existing studies. In this paper, we propose Temporal Graph Learning Recurrent Neural Network (TGLRN) to address these problems. More precisely, to effectively model the nature of time series, we leverage Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to dynamically construct a graph at each time step, thereby capturing the time-evolving spatial dependencies between roads (i.e., microscopic view). Simultaneously, we provide the Adaptive Structure Information to the model, ensuring that close and consecutive sensors are considered to be more important for predicting the traffic flow (i.e., macroscopic view). Furthermore, to endow TGLRN with robustness, we introduce an edge sampling strategy when constructing the graph at each time step, which eventually leads to further improvements on the model performance. Experimental results on four commonly used real-world benchmark datasets show the effectiveness of TGLRN.
source_records.title: Temporal Graph Learning Recurrent Neural Network for Traffic Forecasting

source_records.abstract: Purpose: Over 5M+ people in India rely on Indian Sign Language for communication with specially-abled people, and yet technological support remains very limited. We developed a real-time ISL recognition system as a proof-of-concept demonstrating CPU-based deployment feasibility. Methods: We adapted and optimized existing HWGAT architecture with 9.7M parameters (52.7% reduction from baseline) processing 29 MediaPipe-extracted keypoints enhanced with Fourier features, cyclic shifts, and learnable positional encodings. Our heuristic motion-gated mechanism uses simple displacement thresholds for continuous sign detection. Results: On a limited 6-class dataset (76 samples), the system achieved 78.57% validation accuracy. The 95% CI (49.2%-95.3%) reflects higher variance due to a small sample size, which indicates that the results should be interpreted as preliminary. Ablation studies show that incremental improvements are as such: learnable encodings (+8.33%), Fourier features (+7.14%), and cyclic shifts (+7.14%). Conclusion: Our work demonstrates the feasibility of a CPU-based ISL recognition but acknowledges its significant limitations: a small vocabulary, limited amount of training data and simpler motion-gating heuristics. Findings established baseline for future large-scale studies.

source_records.abstract: Spatial-temporal sequence forecasting (STSF) is a long-standing research problem with widespread real-world applications. The neural architecture search (NAS), which automates neural network design, is essential to adaptively model the correlated dependencies of spatial and temporal features for diverse downstream tasks in STSF. However, existing methods overlook the complex interaction between spatial and temporal operators, which causes a large number of irregular local optima obstructing both heuristic and gradient-based NAS methods. Despite the emerging LLM-based methods improve it with inner knowledge, there still lacks enough mechanism for memory and task decomposed instruction. In this paper, we propose a multilevel enhanced LLM-based NAS method for STSF. Instead of directly question-querying with LLM, we decompose the STSF NAS task into three levels, and inspire the LLM’s capability with an interactive multilevel enhancement mechanism. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves competitive effectiveness against 8 baselines in 5 datasets for STSF.

source_records.abstract: Accurate and computationally efficient prediction of daily financial variables from accounting data is essential for practical industrial applications. In this study, we develop a predictive model based on an Echo State Network (ESN), a representative approach in reservoir computing, using real-world daily accounting datasets. For the task of predicting 31-day ahead cash balances and net working capital, the ESN outperforms the benchmark Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model by 1.324 percentage points in accuracy and surpasses the predictive performance reported in prior studies while achieving approximately 73 times faster training. Furthermore, we conduct a scenario analysis by feeding pseudo journal entries representing future scenarios into the model to examine changes in future financial variables. These results suggest that the ESN is a promising approach for structured accounting time series derived from double-entry bookkeeping, especially when the number of observations is limited, in terms of both predictive accuracy and training efficiency.

source_records.abstract: Spatio-temporal graph neural networks on directed heterogeneous graphs face two structural challenges: symmetric graph aggregations cannot distinguish directional propagation mechanisms, and pure likelihood-based density scoring can underweight sparse localized perturbations. We address both within DA-GTNF, a unified framework for freeway anomaly detection. First, a direction-aware heterogeneous graph explicitly encodes four asymmetric relation types (downstream propagation, upstream shockwave, lateral lane interaction, and diagonal lane change), enabling a Relational GCN to learn independent aggregation kernels per relation. Second, a DualBranchGating mechanism fuses spatial graph embeddings and temporal Transformer embeddings through adaptive, feature-wise gates derived from unfused outputs. Third, a Dual-Conditioned Normalizing Flow estimates exact token-wise conditional log-likelihoods of the gated embeddings, while an auxiliary reconstruction head improves sensitivity to micro-level deviations that may be weakly reflected by NLL alone. On FT-AED, DA-GTNF achieves an AUC of 0.7218, a Reporting Delay of −11.80 min, a Mean Localization Error of 2.23 miles, and 100% incident coverage. On PeMS with incomplete ground truth, the segment-level DA-GTNF variant also consistently improves Recall@K% over all compared baselines.

raw_metadata.abstract: Spatio-temporal graph neural networks on directed heterogeneous graphs face two structural challenges: symmetric graph aggregations cannot distinguish directional propagation mechanisms, and pure likelihood-based density scoring can underweight sparse localized perturbations. We address both within DA-GTNF, a unified framework for freeway anomaly detection. First, a direction-aware heterogeneous graph explicitly encodes four asymmetric relation types (downstream propagation, upstream shockwave, lateral lane interaction, and diagonal lane change), enabling a Relational GCN to learn independent aggregation kernels per relation. Second, a DualBranchGating mechanism fuses spatial graph embeddings and temporal Transformer embeddings through adaptive, feature-wise gates derived from unfused outputs. Third, a Dual-Conditioned Normalizing Flow estimates exact token-wise conditional log-likelihoods of the gated embeddings, while an auxiliary reconstruction head improves sensitivity to micro-level deviations that may be weakly reflected by NLL alone. On FT-AED, DA-GTNF achieves an AUC of 0.7218, a Reporting Delay of −11.80 min, a Mean Localization Error of 2.23 miles, and 100% incident coverage. On PeMS with incomplete ground truth, the segment-level DA-GTNF variant also consistently improves Recall@K% over all compared baselines.

source_records.abstract: 3D skeleton-based gait emotion recognition faces high annotation costs, data scarcity, and poor generalization on heterogeneous data. This paper proposes SV-GCN, a single-stream multi-feature fusion framework with temporal invariance. We introduce intra-frame relative motion features to eliminate frame-rate sensitivity and embed heterogeneous cues at shallow layers, enabling early fusion without multi-stream complexity. For variable-length sequences, we design a global mask-guided valid-frame spatio-temporal graph convolution module, introducing frame-rate insensitivity for the first time in this domain. On the E-Gait dataset, our method achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art while demonstrating strong generalization across varying sequence lengths and frame rates, offering a viable pathway for pre-training on large-scale skeleton-based action recognition datasets. The code will be available at https://github.com/lsr51/SV-GCN .

source_records.abstract: The advancement of intelligent transportation systems (ITS) has necessitated the effective integration of diverse, multi-source traffic data. Conventional approaches reliant on singular structured data struggle to encapsulate the complementarity of diverse modal data, and therefore exhibit limits in intricate traffic environments. In recent years, the cross-modal fusion-based multi-modal knowledge representation learning (KRL) method has significantly improved the semantic depth and resilience of traffic entity representation by amalgamating text, images, time series, and structured graph data. This paper examines the current state of cross-modal data fusion in intelligent transportation, grounded in the theory of multi-source heterogeneous information and knowledge representation learning. It identifies existing technical challenges and explores future avenues for innovation, with the objective of establishing a novel approach to intelligent transportation control driven by KRL. Keywords: intelligent transportation management; knowledge representation learning; multi-source heterogeneous data; cross-modal data integration; massive language model.

source_records.abstract: The rise of large language models (LLMs) has transformed traffic flow prediction in intelligent transportation systems. Unlike traditional methods dependent on structured inputs and handcrafted features, LLMs offer superior semantic reasoning and context modeling, enabling flexible processing of heterogeneous traffic data. This review examines LLM applications in traffic flow prediction, focusing on two paradigms: structure-guided modeling and language-driven generative prediction. We analyze representative models—including TPLLM, ST-LLM, UrbanGPT, and TF-LLM—highlighting their architectures, alignment strategies, and generalization capabilities. The survey also addresses current challenges in structural alignment, zero-shot forecasting, and real-world deployment, providing insights for developing next-generation predictive systems with enhanced interpretability and adaptability.

source_records.abstract: Audio DeepFake detection has advanced significantly in recent years mainly due to competitions like ASVSpoof and ADD; however, these competitions have been focused only on English and Chinese languages; this situation has impacted the field, having fewer experiments performed on other languages. In this paper a focus on detection models to measure their performance across different Spanish datasets, the use of RawBoost data augmentation technique and pre-training on English dataset were explored. A comparison between two popular detection models is presented, mainly the Audio Anti-Spoofing using the Integrated Spectro-Temporal (AASIST) network and Mel-Spectrogram with Residual Network (Spec-ResNet). An evaluation has been conducted on four Spanish deepfake datasets HABLA, HISPASpoof, ODSS and MLAAD in order to assess the cross-dataset generalization capabilities of the models, as well as utilizing the ASVSpoof2019 dataset as a pre-training step is also explored. Results show that the use of RawBoost data augmentation can improve detection metrics, however improvements are minimal and inconsistent across datasets and models, additionally, the pre-trained models on English dataset consistently enhanced metrics on Spanish datasets for AASIST model, and worsen them for the Spec-ResNet model.

An increasing number of machine learning tasks require dealing with large graph datasets, which capture rich and complex relationship among potentially billions of elements. Graph Neural Network (GNN) becomes an effective way to address the graph learning problem by converting the graph data into a low dimensional space while keeping both the structural and property information to the maximum extent and constructing a neural network for training and referencing. However, it is challenging to provide an efficient graph storage and computation capabilities to facilitate GNN training and enable development of new GNN algorithms. In this paper, we present a comprehensive graph neural network system, namely AliGraph, which consists of distributed graph storage, optimized sampling operators and runtime to efficiently support not only existing popular GNNs but also a series of in-house developed ones for different scenarios. The system is currently deployed at Alibaba to support a variety of business scenarios, including product recommendation and personalized search at Alibaba's E-Commerce platform. By conducting extensive experiments on a real-world dataset with 492.90 million vertices, 6.82 billion edges and rich attributes, AliGraph performs an order of magnitude faster in terms of graph building (5 minutes vs hours reported from the state-of-the-art PowerGraph platform). At training, AliGraph runs 40%-50% faster with the novel caching strategy and demonstrates around 12 times speed up with the improved runtime. In addition, our in-house developed GNN models all showcase their statistically significant superiorities in terms of both effectiveness and efficiency (e.g., 4.12%-17.19% lift by F1 scores).

Machine learning over graphs have been emerging as powerful learning tools for graph data. However, it is challenging for industrial communities to leverage the techniques, such as graph neural networks (GNNs), and solve real-world problems at scale because of inherent data dependency in the graphs. As such, we cannot simply train a GNN with classic learning systems, for instance parameter server that assumes data parallel. Existing systems store the graph data in-memory for fast accesses either in a single machine or graph stores from remote. The major drawbacks are in three-fold. First, they cannot scale because of the limitations on the volume of the memory, or the bandwidth between graph stores and workers. Second, they require extra development of graph stores without well exploiting mature infrastructures such as MapReduce that guarantee good system properties. Third, they focus on training but ignore the optimization of inference over graphs, thus makes them an unintegrated system.
  In this paper, we design AGL, a scalable, fault-tolerance and integrated system, with fully-functional training and inference for GNNs. Our system design follows the message passing scheme underlying the computations of GNNs. We design to generate the $k$-hop neighborhood, an information-complete subgraph for each node, as well as do the inference simply by merging values from in-edge neighbors and propagating values to out-edge neighbors via MapReduce. In addition, the $k$-hop neighborhood contains information-complete subgraphs for each node, thus we simply do the training on parameter servers due to data independency. Our system AGL, implemented on mature infrastructures, can finish the training of a 2-layer graph attention network on a graph with billions of nodes and hundred billions of edges in 14 hours, and complete the inference in 1.2 hour.

Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) are powerful models for learning representations of attributed graphs. To scale GCNs to large graphs, state-of-the-art methods use various layer sampling techniques to alleviate the "neighbor explosion" problem during minibatch training. We propose GraphSAINT, a graph sampling based inductive learning method that improves training efficiency and accuracy in a fundamentally different way. By changing perspective, GraphSAINT constructs minibatches by sampling the training graph, rather than the nodes or edges across GCN layers. Each iteration, a complete GCN is built from the properly sampled subgraph. Thus, we ensure fixed number of well-connected nodes in all layers. We further propose normalization technique to eliminate bias, and sampling algorithms for variance reduction. Importantly, we can decouple the sampling from the forward and backward propagation, and extend GraphSAINT with many architecture variants (e.g., graph attention, jumping connection). GraphSAINT demonstrates superior performance in both accuracy and training time on five large graphs, and achieves new state-of-the-art F1 scores for PPI (0.995) and Reddit (0.970).

The graph convolutional networks (GCN) recently proposed by Kipf and Welling are an effective graph model for semi-supervised learning. This model, however, was originally designed to be learned with the presence of both training and test data. Moreover, the recursive neighborhood expansion across layers poses time and memory challenges for training with large, dense graphs. To relax the requirement of simultaneous availability of test data, we interpret graph convolutions as integral transforms of embedding functions under probability measures. Such an interpretation allows for the use of Monte Carlo approaches to consistently estimate the integrals, which in turn leads to a batched training scheme as we propose in this work---FastGCN. Enhanced with importance sampling, FastGCN not only is efficient for training but also generalizes well for inference. We show a comprehensive set of experiments to demonstrate its effectiveness compared with GCN and related models. In particular, training is orders of magnitude more efficient while predictions remain comparably accurate.

We present graph attention networks (GATs), novel neural network architectures that operate on graph-structured data, leveraging masked self-attentional layers to address the shortcomings of prior methods based on graph convolutions or their approximations. By stacking layers in which nodes are able to attend over their neighborhoods' features, we enable (implicitly) specifying different weights to different nodes in a neighborhood, without requiring any kind of costly matrix operation (such as inversion) or depending on knowing the graph structure upfront. In this way, we address several key challenges of spectral-based graph neural networks simultaneously, and make our model readily applicable to inductive as well as transductive problems. Our GAT models have achieved or matched state-of-the-art results across four established transductive and inductive graph benchmarks: the Cora, Citeseer and Pubmed citation network datasets, as well as a protein-protein interaction dataset (wherein test graphs remain unseen during training).

source_records.abstract: Compositional predictors, such as microbiome abundances, pose unique challenges in variable selection due to their unit-sum constraint and inherent dependencies. Existing approaches often rely on fixed association graphs derived from phylogenetic or ecological distances, which may not reflect outcome-relevant relationships. We propose GRACE (GRaph-Adaptive horseshoe for Compositional rEgression), a fully Bayesian framework that enforces compositional constraints, performs variable selection, and adaptively learns an outcome-driven shrinkage graph. GRACE achieves compositionality through a novel linear reparameterization of regression coefficients, while a structured horseshoe prior induces sparsity and smooths coefficients along the learned graph. Graph learning is accomplished via scaled beta2 priors on edge weights, providing both outcome-specific adaptation and posterior uncertainty quantification. We develop an efficient Gibbs sampler incorporating elliptical slice sampling to ensure scalability in high dimensions. Through extensive simulations, GRACE demonstrates competitive predictive accuracy and improved graph recovery compared with existing methods, particularly under graph misspecification. Application to oral microbiome data from the ORIGINS study identifies taxa associated with insulin resistance and yields an outcome-driven graph summarizing how those taxa relate to the outcome, a structure that differs substantially from phylogenetic or co-occurrence networks. These findings highlight that fixed predictor graphs useful for regularization may not faithfully represent outcome-relevant feature relationships, underscoring the need for adaptive, outcome-informed approaches in compositional regression.
source_records.title: Graph-Adaptive Horseshoe for Compositional Regression

source_records.abstract: Given a large graph, how to generate a compact summary graph that is configurable by the user and supports multiple graph queries with either no loss or with high accuracy? The ever growing size of graph datasets makes the above question on graph summarization very pertinent. Although, there are several approaches, there does not exist a configurable graph summarization method that offers high compression along with support for multiple graph queries on the summary graph with high accuracy, and allows the user to configure the summarization based on: (1) lossless or lossy summarization, (2) amount of tolerable neighborhood loss, (3) the type of loss it can tolerate, in terms of false positive edges (i.e., extra edges), false negative edges (i.e., missing edges), or neither, in both the (a) reconstructed graph and the (b) query answers. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel graph summarization framework CGS (Configurable Graph Summarizer) that builds upon the idea of aggregating nodes with common neighborhoods. The CGS framework consists of three summarization variants, CGS-E, CGS-I and CGS-U. While CGS-E is a lossless scheme, CGS-I and CGS-U are lossy schemes that allow reconstruction of the input graph with no false positive edges and no false negative edges, respectively. To bound the graph reconstruction loss, we introduce a user-specified parameter neighborhood loss tolerance threshold, that limits the maximum loss allowed in the neighborhood of each node. This allows graph reconstruction and neighborhood query evaluation with either no loss or with bounded loss guarantees. Empirical evaluation on several synthetic and real-world graphs shows that CGS offers superior summarization than the state-of-the-art methods, and can answer graph queries with fairly high accuracy and efficiency.
source_records.title: CGS: Configurable Graph Summarization with Bounded Neighborhood Loss and Query Support

source_records.abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are extensively used across different domains and in several applications. Often, these KGs are very large in size. Such KGs become unwieldy for tasks such as question answering and visualization. Summarization of KGs offers a viable alternative in such cases. Furthermore, personalized KG summarization is crucial in the current data-driven world as it captures the specific requirements of users based on their query patterns. Since it only maintains relevant information, the personalized summaries of KG are small, resulting in significantly smaller storage requirements and query runtime. In this work, we adapt the coreset theory to create personalized KG summaries. For a given dataset and a user-specific query workload, we present an approach that samples a relevant subset of triples using sensitivity-based importance sampling. We ensure that the subset approximates the characteristics of the full dataset with bounded approximation error. We define sensitivity scores that measure the importance of a triple with respect to a user's query workload, which are then used by our coreset construction algorithm. We explicitly focus on personalized knowledge graph summarization by constructing summaries independently for each user based on their query behaviour. Our evaluation on Freebase, WikiData, and DBpedia shows that COREKG delivers higher query-answering accuracy and structural coverage than the state-of-the-art methods, such as GLIMPSE, PPR, iSummary, PEGASUS and APEX$^2$ while requiring only a tiny fraction of the original graph.
source_records.title: COREKG: Coreset-Guided Personalized Summarization of Knowledge Graphs

source_records.abstract: Spectral-based machine learning models have been increasingly deployed in chemometrics and spectroscopy, where predictive accuracy is as important as explainability. Current employed eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods are largely adapted from tabular or generic multivariate domains, assigning relevance to isolated spectral variables rather than to the chemically meaningful spectral zones. Widely adopted tools such as SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Permutation Feature Importance (PFI), and Variable Importance in Projection scores (VIP) were not designed for the physical continuity and high collinearity of spectral data, and their variable-level outputs require post-hoc aggregation to recover zone-level information. This study introduces the Spectral Model eXplainer (SMX), a post-hoc, global, model-agnostic XAI framework that explains spectral classifiers through expert-informed spectral zones. SMX summarizes each zone via PCA, defines quantile-based logical predicates, estimates predicate relevance with perturbation in stochastic subsamples, and aggregates bag-wise rankings in a directed weighted graph summarized by Local Reaching Centrality. A key component is threshold spectrum reconstruction, which back-projects predicate boundaries to the original spectral domain in natural measurement units, enabling direct visual comparison with measured spectra. The method was evaluated on eight real spectral datasets (six based on X-ray Fluorescence--XRF and two based on Gamma-ray Spectrometry) and one synthetic benchmark with known gr
source_records.title: Spectral Model eXplainer: a chemically-grounded explainability framework for spectral-based machine learning models

source_records.abstract: The Mapper algorithm from topological data analysis constructs a graph summarizing the shape of a high-dimensional dataset, and groups of data points identified within this graph are widely interpreted as evidence of distinct subtypes. However, the covariance structure of the data alone can make such groups appear differentiated, even when no subtypes are present. Existing validation approaches do not account for this effect and thus cannot distinguish covariance artifacts from genuine subtypes. We propose a Gaussian null model that generates reference data matching the sample covariance matrix. We pair it with a test statistic that measures mean-level differentiation between communities. In an idealized setting, we prove that covariance geometry alone causes Mapper communities to differ in their average feature profiles, and we show that a simpler label-permutation baseline cannot detect this effect. Simulations confirm well-controlled Type I error under Gaussian data. We apply the framework to four published Mapper analyses spanning breast cancer gene expression, Congressional voting, NBA player performance, and lower-grade glioma genomics. In every case, once outlier singleton communities are accounted for, the observed differentiation does not exceed what the null produces at the α = 0.05 level. This result does not rule out subtypes in these datasets, but it does indicate that the observed structure is consistent with what covariance geometry alone can produce. Stronger evidence would be needed to support a subtype claim.
source_records.title: A Null Model for Mapper Subtype Claims

source_records.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) produce high-dimensional embeddings that capture rich semantic and syntactic relationships between words, sentences, and concepts. Investigating the topological structures of LLM embedding spaces via mapper graphs enables us to understand their underlying structures. Specifically, a mapper graph summarizes the topological structure of the embedding space, where each node represents a topological neighborhood (containing a cluster of embeddings), and an edge connects two nodes if their corresponding neighborhoods overlap. However, manually exploring these embedding spaces to uncover encoded linguistic properties requires considerable human effort. To address this challenge, we introduce a framework for semi-automatic annotation of these embedding properties. To organize the exploration process, we first define a taxonomy of explorable elements within a mapper graph such as nodes, edges, paths, components, and trajectories. The annotation of these elements is executed through two types of customizable LLM-based agents that employ perturbation techniques for scalable and automated analysis. These agents help to explore and explain the characteristics of mapper elements and verify the robustness of the generated explanations. We instantiate the framework within a visual analytics workspace and demonstrate its effectiveness through case studies. In particular, we replicate findings from prior research on BERT's embedding properties across various layers of its architecture and provide further observations into the linguistic properties of topological neighborhoods.
source_records.title: Explainable Mapper: Charting LLM Embedding Spaces Using Perturbation-Based Explanation and Verification Agents

source_records.abstract: Causal inference aids researchers in discovering cause-and-effect relationships, leading to scientific insights. Accurate causal estimation requires identifying confounding variables to avoid false discoveries. Pearl's causal model uses causal DAGs to identify confounding variables, but incorrect DAGs can lead to unreliable causal conclusions. However, for high dimensional data, the causal DAGs are often complex beyond human verifiability. Graph summarization is a logical next step, but current methods for general-purpose graph summarization are inadequate for causal DAG summarization. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a causal graph summarization objective that balances graph simplification for better understanding while retaining essential causal information for reliable inference. We develop an efficient greedy algorithm and show that summary causal DAGs can be directly used for inference and are more robust to misspecification of assumptions, enhancing robustness for causal inference. Experimenting with six real-life datasets, we compared our algorithm to three existing solutions, showing its effectiveness in handling high-dimensional data and its ability to generate summary DAGs that ensure both reliable causal inference and robustness against misspecifications.
source_records.title: Causal DAG Summarization (Full Version)

source_records.abstract: Understanding and navigating large-scale codebases remains a significant challenge in software engineering. Existing methods often treat code as flat text or focus primarily on local structural relationships, limiting their ability to provide holistic, context-aware information retrieval. We present Hierarchical Code Graph Summarization (HCGS), a novel approach that constructs a multi-layered representation of a codebase by generating structured summaries in a bottom-up fashion from a code graph. HCGS leverages the Language Server Protocol for language-agnostic code analysis and employs a parallel level-based algorithm for efficient summary generation. Through extensive evaluation on five diverse codebases totaling 7,531 functions, HCGS demonstrates significant improvements in code retrieval accuracy, achieving up to 82 percentage relative improvement in top-1 retrieval precision for large codebases like libsignal (27.15 percentage points), and perfect Pass@3 scores for smaller repositories. The system's hierarchical approach consistently outperforms traditional code-only retrieval across all metrics, with particularly substantial gains in larger, more complex codebases where understanding function relationships is crucial.
source_records.title: Code-Craft: Hierarchical Graph-Based Code Summarization for Enhanced Context Retrieval
